# Create a capital deposit case

Create a <Term id="capital-deposit">capital deposit</Term> case for a new company with the API. One call starts onboarding for the main company and all shareholders.

:::caution Multi-step process
This page covers the first part of a multi-step process:

1. Create the capital deposit case.
1. Complete company and shareholder onboarding.
1. Complete identity and [account holder verification](/accounts/concepts/account-holders/verification).
1. Upload the required documents.

The mutation creates the case and the related onboardings. It doesn't complete onboarding, verification, document review, or capital transfers.

Refer to [Manage a capital deposit case](/accounts/guides/capital-deposits/deposit-capital) for the full operational process.
:::

Use the access token and the [endpoint](/build#endpoints) of the environment you're working in, Sandbox or Live.

## Overview {#overview}

The [`createCapitalDeposit`](https://api-reference.swan.io/mutations/create-capital-deposit) mutation is the new entry point for capital deposits. It replaces the deprecated `createCapitalDepositCase` mutation.

A single call creates:

- One onboarding for the main company being formed.
- One onboarding for each company shareholder, if any.
- One onboarding for each individual shareholder, if any.

Send all shareholder data in the initial request: this mutation is designed for one complete submission.
You can [update a company onboarding](/accounts/guides/onboarding/company/update) or [update an individual onboarding](/accounts/guides/onboarding/individual/update) to make corrections, but updates aren't the intended path for building a case incrementally.

:::info Partner experience
The response includes an `onboardingUrl` for the future company and for each shareholder.

Expose the relevant URL through your partner experience so that the company administrator and shareholders can complete their onboarding. Store each onboarding ID so that you can monitor progress and retrieve validation errors.

A successful `createCapitalDeposit` response doesn't mean that onboarding or <Term id="kyc">KYC</Term> is complete. Continue monitoring each onboarding and account holder status.
:::

The mutation accepts three top-level fields:

```graphql
createCapitalDeposit(input: {
  acquisitionChannel: ...     # How you acquired the user
  mainCompany: { ... }        # The company being incorporated
  shareholders: [ ... ]       # One entry per shareholder
})
```

Each entry in `shareholders` must contain exactly one of `company` or `individual`:

```graphql
{ company: { ... } }      # Company shareholder
{ individual: { ... } }   # Individual shareholder
```

## Step 1: Prepare your data {#prepare}

Collect the following information for each entity before calling the mutation.

<FieldRequirementsLegend />

On this page, <Req /> means the mutation rejects the call without the field.
<Cnd /> means the mutation accepts the call without the field, but Swan sets the onboarding status to `Invalid` until you add it.
Query `statusInfo.errors` on each onboarding before finalizing it, then update the onboarding with the missing values.

For every account, the account name is optional.
If you don't set one, Swan uses `dépôt de capital — <holder name>` by default.

**Main company**

| Data to prepare | Requirement | API field |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| Company name | <Req /> | `mainCompany.company.name` |
| Trade name | <Opt /> | `mainCompany.company.tradeName` |
| Legal form code | <Cnd /> | `mainCompany.company.legalFormCode` |
| Registration number | <Opt /> | `mainCompany.company.registrationNumber` |
| Registered address | <Cnd /> | `mainCompany.company.address` |
| Business activity | <Cnd /> | `mainCompany.company.businessActivity`, `mainCompany.company.businessActivityCode`, `mainCompany.company.businessActivityDescription` |
| Account admin | <Req /> | `mainCompany.accountAdmin` |
| <Term id="ubo">UBOs</Term> and <Term id="legal-representative">legal representatives</Term> | <Cnd /> | `mainCompany.company.relatedIndividuals` |
| Account name | <Opt /> | `mainCompany.accountInfo.name` |
| Redirect URL | <Req /> | `mainCompany.oAuthRedirectParameters.redirectUrl` |

The main company isn't incorporated yet, so its registration number is optional.

**Each company shareholder**

| Data to prepare | Requirement | API field |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| Capital deposit amount | <Req /> | `shareholders[].company.capitalDepositAmount` |
| Company name | <Req /> | `shareholders[].company.company.name` |
| Trade name | <Opt /> | `shareholders[].company.company.tradeName` |
| Legal form code | <Cnd /> | `shareholders[].company.company.legalFormCode` |
| Registration number | <Cnd /> | `shareholders[].company.company.registrationNumber` |
| Registered address | <Cnd /> | `shareholders[].company.company.address` |
| Business activity | <Cnd /> | `shareholders[].company.company.businessActivity`, `shareholders[].company.company.businessActivityCode`, `shareholders[].company.company.businessActivityDescription` |
| Account admin | <Req /> | `shareholders[].company.accountAdmin` |
| UBOs and legal representatives | <Cnd /> | `shareholders[].company.company.relatedIndividuals` |
| Account name | <Opt /> | `shareholders[].company.accountInfo.name` |
| Redirect URL | <Req /> | `shareholders[].company.oAuthRedirectParameters.redirectUrl` |

Company shareholders are registered legal entities, so include their registration number.

:::tip Pre-fill for French companies
For company shareholders registered in France, use the `companyInfoRegistryData` query with the company's registration number to retrieve data from the National Business Register (RNE).
Pass the results to the mutation to pre-fill company fields.
:::

For complete field-level requirements and required-document rules, see [Company onboarding fields](/accounts/reference/onboarding/company-onboarding-fields).

**Each individual shareholder**

| Data to prepare | Requirement | API field |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| Capital contribution | <Req /> | `shareholders[].individual.capitalDepositAmount` |
| First and last name | <Req /> | `shareholders[].individual.accountAdmin.firstName` and `lastName` |
| Date and place of birth | <Req /> | `shareholders[].individual.accountAdmin.birthInfo` |
| Nationality | <Req /> | `shareholders[].individual.accountAdmin.nationality` |
| Address | <Cnd /> | `shareholders[].individual.accountAdmin.address` |
| Employment status and income | <Cnd /> | `shareholders[].individual.accountAdmin.employmentStatus` and `monthlyIncome` |
| FATCA information | <Cnd /> | `shareholders[].individual.accountAdmin.unitedStatesTaxInfo` |
| Account name | <Opt /> | `shareholders[].individual.accountInfo.name` |
| Redirect URL | <Req /> | `shareholders[].individual.oAuthRedirectParameters.redirectUrl` |

For complete field-level requirements and required-document rules, see [Individual onboarding fields](/accounts/reference/onboarding/individual-onboarding-fields).

### Find valid legal form codes {#legal-forms}

Use the `legalForms` query to get all valid legal form codes for a country, with localized names and abbreviations.

<a href="https://explorer.swan.io?query=cXVlcnkgR2V0TGVnYWxGb3JtcyB7CiAgbGVnYWxGb3Jtcyhjb3VudHJ5OiAiRlJBIikgewogICAgY29kZQogICAgY291bnRyeQogICAgbG9jYWxOYW1lCiAgICBsb2NhbEFiYnJldmlhdGlvbgogIH0KfQo%3D&tab=api" className="explorer-badge">Open in API Explorer</a>

```graphql
query GetLegalForms {
  legalForms(country: "FRA") {
    code
    country
    localName
    localAbbreviation
  }
}
```

### Model UBOs across the ownership structure {#ubo-modeling}

When a company is a shareholder of the company being incorporated, declare UBOs at both company levels:

1. Declare the UBOs of the company shareholder in `shareholders[].company.company.relatedIndividuals`.
1. Declare the individuals who ultimately own the main company, directly or through a company shareholder, in `mainCompany.company.relatedIndividuals`.

The same individual can appear in both places, but calculate the ownership percentage relative to the entity being described.

```
MyBrand
├── 50% owned directly by Henri Dupont
└── 50% owned by MyBrand Company Shareholder
    └── 100% owned by Jules Fleury
```

| Individual | Entity | Relationship | Percentage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Henri Dupont | MyBrand | Direct UBO | 50% |
| Jules Fleury | MyBrand | Indirect UBO through the company shareholder | 50% |
| Jules Fleury | MyBrand Company Shareholder | Direct UBO | 100% |

The percentage in the main company UBO entry is the person's effective ownership of the main company.
It's not necessarily the percentage they hold in the intermediate company.
For example, if an intermediate company owns 50% of the main company and an individual owns 60% of that intermediate company, the individual's indirect ownership of the main company is 30%.

A legal representative isn't automatically a UBO.
Choose the `type` that matches the individual's roles:

- `UltimateBeneficialOwner` for a UBO only.
- `LegalRepresentative` for a legal representative only.
- `LegalRepresentativeAndUltimateBeneficialOwner` when the same individual has both roles.

:::caution `relatedCompanies` doesn't model ownership
Only use `relatedCompanies` when a legal entity acts as the legal representative of another company.
Represent shareholder ownership through the shareholder company and its `relatedIndividuals`.
:::

## Step 2: Call the mutation {#call-mutation}

The following example shows a case with one company shareholder and one individual shareholder.

### Mutation {#mutation}

<a href="https://explorer.swan.io?%3D%3D&tab=api" className="explorer-badge">Open in API Explorer</a>

```graphql {276,288,304,307} showLineNumbers
    __typename

    ... on CreateCapitalDepositSuccessPayload {
      capitalDepositCase {

          value

        companyOnboarding {
          id
          onboardingUrl
          statusInfo {
            status
            validationVersion
            ... on OnboardingInvalidStatusInfo {
              errors {
                details
                errors
                field
              }
            }
          }
        }

        shareholders {
          id
          status
          onboarding {
            id
            onboardingUrl
            statusInfo {
              status
              validationVersion
              ... on OnboardingInvalidStatusInfo {
                errors {
                  details
                  errors
                  field
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }

    ... on CapitalDepositShareholdersEmptyRejection {
      message
    }

    ... on CapitalDepositMainCompanyOnboardingRejection {
      message
      fields {
        message
        path
      }
    }

    ... on CapitalDepositShareholderOnboardingRejection {
      message
      fields {
        message
        path
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Payload {#payload}

The success payload returns the case, the main company onboarding, and one entry per shareholder, in the order you sent them.
The highlighted lines are the IDs to store: the case (line 6), the main company onboarding (line 15), and each shareholder with its onboarding (lines 24, 27, 36, and 39).
Every onboarding in this example is `Valid`, so no `errors` array is returned.

```json {6,15,24,27,36,39} showLineNumbers
{
  "data": {
    "createCapitalDeposit": {
      "__typename": "CreateCapitalDepositSuccessPayload",
      "capitalDepositCase": {
        "id": "a4c9da36-56e1-4ed8-b0a1-2c9f3d7e8b12",
        "statusInfo": {
          "status": "WaitingForInitialRequirements"
        },
```

## Step 3: Store IDs and check onboarding status {#store-ids}

From a successful response, store:

- `capitalDepositCase.id`: your reference for the full case.
- `capitalDepositCase.companyOnboarding.id`: to track the main company onboarding. Also store `onboardingUrl` to redirect your user, unless your integration is API-only.
- `shareholders[].onboarding.id`: to track each shareholder onboarding. Also store each `onboardingUrl`, unless your integration is API-only.

A successful mutation doesn't mean every onboarding is ready to be finalized.

:::caution Check every onboarding status
Always check `statusInfo.status` on `companyOnboarding` and on each `shareholders[].onboarding`.

Completing onboarding doesn't guarantee that account holder verification is complete. Swan may request additional information during KYC, so continue monitoring the account holder status after you finalize the onboarding.

Swan can create an onboarding with the status `Invalid` when a required field is missing.

Refer to [Get onboarding info](/accounts/guides/onboarding/manage-onboardings/get-info), read the `errors` array, and fix the issue before you finalize the onboarding.
:::

Example of a case created with an invalid onboarding:

```json
{
  "capitalDepositCase": {
    "statusInfo": { "status": "WaitingForInitialRequirements" },
    "companyOnboarding": {
      "statusInfo": {
        "status": "Invalid",
        "validationVersion": "V2",
        "errors": [
          {
            "field": "company.legalFormCode",
            "details": "Invalid input: expected string, received null"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

:::info Required documents per onboarding
The documents needed to complete an onboarding depend on the entity and context.
Before asking your user to complete the flow, [list the required documents](/accounts/guides/onboarding/manage-onboardings/list-required-documents) for each onboarding.
:::

## Step 4: Complete onboarding and KYC {#kyc}

After your users [finalize their onboardings](/accounts/guides/onboarding/manage-onboardings/finalize), the KYC process for each entity begins with the identification of each account admin (the first account membership, with `legalRepresentative: true`).

## Step 5: Upload required documents {#upload}

The [capital deposit reference](/accounts/reference/capital-deposits#documents-list) lists the required documents by stakeholder, who supplies each one, and where it's attached.

After you create the case, its status is `WaitingForInitialRequirements`.
It stays in this status until every [initial requirement](/accounts/concepts/capital-deposits/statuses#case) is complete, including the upload of all required documents, and then moves to `PendingInternalReview`.

Document upload and KYC happen in parallel, so you don't need to wait for shareholders to finish their onboarding.
Start uploading as soon as the documents are available.

If Swan refuses a document, review its refusal reason and upload a corrected version, as described in [Upload required documents](/accounts/guides/capital-deposits/upload-documents#replace-refused).

The case and each shareholder have a `documents` array with pre-assigned document IDs and types.
Query the case for the document IDs. Then [upload each document](/accounts/guides/capital-deposits/upload-documents) using the two-step signed URL flow.

### Query {#documents-query}

<a href="https://explorer.swan.io?&tab=api" className="explorer-badge">Open in API Explorer</a>

```graphql {4,11,13} showLineNumbers
query GetCapitalDepositDocuments {
  capitalDepositCase(id: "$YOUR_CAPITALDEPOSITCASE_ID") {
    documents {
      id
      type
      statusInfo {
        status
      }
    }
    shareholders {
      id
      documents {
        id
        type
        statusInfo {
          status
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Payload {#documents-payload}

Each document placeholder is created with the status `Pending`.
The highlighted lines are the document IDs to store: case documents (lines 6, 13, and 20) and the individual shareholder's proof of address (line 36).
The company shareholder has an empty `documents` array because Swan collects its registry extract during onboarding.

```json {6,13,20,36} showLineNumbers
{
  "data": {
    "capitalDepositCase": {
      "documents": [
        {
          "id": "0a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c01",
          "type": "ArticlesOfIncorporation",
          "statusInfo": {
            "status": "Pending"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "1b2c3d4e-5f6a-4b7c-9d8e-0f1a2b3c4d02",
          "type": "CompanyLeaseAgreement",
          "statusInfo": {
            "status": "Pending"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "2c3d4e5f-6a7b-4c8d-8e9f-1a2b3c4d5e03",
          "type": "PowerOfAttorney",
          "statusInfo": {
            "status": "Pending"
          }
        }
      ],
      "shareholders": [
        {
          "id": "8b1e6f2a-0c3d-4a5b-8e9f-6a7b8c9d0e11",
          "documents": []
        },
        {
          "id": "d4e5f6a7-b8c9-4d0e-9f1a-2b3c4d5e6f33",
          "documents": [
            {
              "id": "3d4e5f6a-7b8c-4d9e-9f0a-2b3c4d5e6f04",
              "type": "ProofOfIndividualAddress",
              "statusInfo": {
                "status": "Pending"
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Rejections {#rejections}

| Rejection type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `CapitalDepositShareholdersEmptyRejection` | No shareholder was provided. |
| `CapitalDepositMainCompanyOnboardingRejection` | The main company onboarding data is invalid. |
| `CapitalDepositShareholderOnboardingRejection` | A shareholder onboarding entry is invalid. |

The `fields` array in each rejection identifies the exact field and path causing the error:

```json
{
  "__typename": "CapitalDepositShareholderOnboardingRejection",
```

## Changes from the deprecated mutation {#whats-new}

`createCapitalDeposit` replaces the monolithic `onboardingInfo` block from `createCapitalDepositCase` with structured, per-entity inputs aligned with the standard [Swan onboarding](/accounts/guides/onboarding) format.
For the deprecated mutation, see [Create a capital deposit case (deprecated)](/accounts/guides/capital-deposits/create-case).

| Deprecated (`createCapitalDepositCase`) | New (`createCapitalDeposit`) |
| --- | --- |
| `companyShareholders[].onboardingInfo` | `shareholders[].company` with `accountInfo`, `accountAdmin`, `company`, and `oAuthRedirectParameters` |
| `individualShareholders[].onboardingInfo` | `shareholders[].individual` with `accountInfo`, `accountAdmin`, and `oAuthRedirectParameters` |
| `onboardingInfo.accountName` | `accountInfo.name` |
| `representatives` | `company.relatedIndividuals[]` with the type `LegalRepresentative` |
| `individualUltimateBeneficialOwners` | `company.relatedIndividuals[]` with the type `UltimateBeneficialOwner` |
| `direct` and `indirect` booleans | `ownership.type` (`Direct` or `Indirect`) and `ownership.totalPercentage` |
| `language` | `accountAdmin.preferredLanguage` |
